articles.title: Interior designers agree: this one colour makes any living room feel instantly more refined
articles.excerpt: "People want emotion, and colour creates it," one designer explains.
articles.author: anabel-blazquez
articles.imageCaption: A living room styled in a warm, muted tone | EP
content: Interior designers say a single muted, earthy tone has become the most requested choice for living rooms this year.
"People want emotion, and colour creates it," one designer explains, noting that clients are moving away from stark neutrals toward warmer, more grounded palettes.
The shift mirrors a broader trend toward rooms that feel lived-in rather than showroom-perfect.

articles.title: Small-kitchen storage is the design problem everyone is trying to solve this year
articles.excerpt: As flats shrink, designers say clever vertical storage has replaced open shelving as the must-have feature.
articles.author: anabel-blazquez
articles.imageCaption: A compact kitchen with floor-to-ceiling cabinetry | EP
content: As new-build flats trend smaller, kitchen designers say demand has shifted decisively toward vertical, floor-to-ceiling storage solutions.
Open shelving, popular for much of the last decade, is losing ground to closed cabinetry that hides clutter in tighter spaces.
Several designers note that clients are now willing to pay a premium for custom joinery that makes full use of awkward corners.

articles.title: Balcony gardens are booming as city dwellers reclaim outdoor space
articles.excerpt: Garden centres report a sharp rise in sales of compact planters designed for balconies under four square metres.
articles.author: anabel-blazquez
articles.imageCaption: A small balcony filled with potted plants | EP
content: Garden centres across the country are reporting a sharp rise in sales of compact planters and vertical growing systems designed specifically for small balconies.
Retailers say the trend accelerated after several years of flat sizes shrinking, pushing residents to treat balconies as a primary outdoor space rather than an afterthought.
Landscape designers now offer balcony-specific consultations, a service that barely existed five years ago.

articles.title: Second-hand furniture is having a moment, and it's not just about saving money
articles.excerpt: Buyers cite sustainability and character as much as price when explaining the shift away from flat-pack.
articles.author: victor-lenore
articles.imageCaption: A restored wooden sideboard in a showroom | EP
content: Sales of second-hand and restored furniture have grown steadily over the past two years, according to several online marketplaces and dealers.
Buyers surveyed cite sustainability and a desire for pieces with character as much as price when explaining their move away from flat-pack furniture.
Restorers say demand for reupholstery and refinishing services has grown alongside the trend, with waiting lists at several workshops stretching past two months.

articles.title: Bathroom renovations are trading tile patterns for minimalist, single-tone finishes
articles.excerpt: Contractors say the shift is partly aesthetic and partly practical: fewer materials mean fewer things to source and match.
articles.author: anabel-blazquez
articles.imageCaption: A minimalist bathroom with a single-tone tile finish | EP
content: Bathroom renovations this year have leaned heavily toward minimalist, single-tone finishes, a departure from the patterned tile schemes popular in recent years.
Contractors say the shift is partly aesthetic and partly practical, since using fewer materials means fewer things to source, match and eventually replace.
Designers add that the simpler palettes also tend to make small bathrooms feel larger, a persistent concern in older housing stock.
